Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced an authoritative ITU figure. The ITU Digital Development Dashboard for Eritrea records international internet bandwidth of 8 kbit/s per internet user, dated 2017 — the most recent figure available, since Eritrea has not submitted updated ITU telecommunications data since 2017 (confirmed by a 2026 ITU data-availability review). This places Eritrea in category 2 (Low, 5-19 kbit/s). Score changed from Unknown to 2, though the underlying figure is nearly a decade old and should be treated cautiously.
revised_comments: Eritrea's international internet bandwidth stood at 8 kbit/s per internet user according to the ITU Digital Development Dashboard, the most recent figure published for the country. Eritrea has not submitted updated telecommunications data to the ITU since 2017; the country's international connectivity depends on a state-controlled gateway with indirect access to regional submarine cable systems.
